name: Cloisonnism
summary: Flat areas of one colour held by a dark outline, as the lead holds the glass in a church window.
how: Fill each shape with one flat colour and no gradient.
Draw a dark contour of 3 to 8mm round each shape.
Set a few large shapes against a high horizon, with no cast shadow.

origin.note: Louis Anquetin and Émile Bernard paint flat, outlined shapes in Paris; the critic Édouard Dujardin names the manner in 1888.

adoptions.via: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, a friend of Anquetin and Bernard, prints flat fields of colour with a dark outline in the lithograph poster Moulin Rouge: La Goulue.
